# feat(budget): the cost meter and the pageOverBudget refusal at publish

<!-- bogd3v/micelio-plugin-core#46 as read with gh issue view on 2026-10-24: the input of micelio-plugin-core-46.md -->

Part of #62.

## Why

A budget that is only measured in CI arrives after the page is written. The builder's promise is that an editor sees the weight while writing and cannot publish over it (success criterion: 0 pages that fail a budget at publish).

## What to build

- `server/src/services/budget.ts`: the budget per page type and site from configuration (decision 7: configuration only; the core ships neutral defaults, `landing` 60 kB, `standard` 120 kB, `long-read` 160 kB, overridable in `config/plugins`), `measure(document)` calling the frontend's weight report.
- The cost meter component (`admin/src/components/CostMeter.tsx`) in the preview pane: total against the budget, on-demand weight apart, the colour changing at 90 % and 100 % (not along the way), per-block breakdown on expand.
- The editorial transition to `published` runs the measurement and refuses with `pageOverBudget` (problem detail, `application/problem+json`, the blocks over and by how much); the refusal reaches the Content Manager as a notification with a link to the preview page.
- `docs/api.md` (the error), `docs/operate/budgets.md`.

## Requirements

- Measurement is the frontend's; the plugin never estimates. If the frontend is unreachable the transition is refused with `previewUnavailable`, never allowed by default.
- The refusal holds through the content API and the hooks, not only in the admin (a `publish` through Strapi's native button is refused too: the server decides).
- `feat` → MINOR; a new problem detail code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Integration: a seeded page over its budget cannot be published through the admin route nor through the Document Service; under it, it can.
- [ ] Unit: the meter's thresholds and the on-demand separation.
- [ ] The browser suite sees the meter turn at 90 % with the seeded heavy page.
- [ ] Verified by the maintainer on the plugin's Docker Compose (`compose.dev.yml`: clean Strapi with the plugin, PostgreSQL and the frontend image), following the steps the PR lists under Tests.
